correctness.rationale: For each fit the active equality forest yields a connected-block averaging map. Every connected block partition has a strictly complementary KKT witness on an open affine region; the forest-incidence rows are independent. Because cut indicators form an exact ℓ1 basis for tree variation modulo constants, the variation operator norm of each block averaging map is the largest image of one edge cut; computing this image gives (bp+aq)/(a+b). A finite-selection argument proves the global upper bound, and the strict KKT regions prove matching local lower bounds. Connected-side knapsack computes the maximizing value. Direct counting proves paths/stars/cubic-caterpillar formulas. The exact rational checker separately corroborated connected-subtree and partition variants on 20 trees, 1504 exact KKT witnesses and four side-profile tests; no finite test is treated as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the intrinsic perturbation stability of Euclidean isotonic fitting under the natural graph gradient seminorm. The result solves the full finite-tree case by an exact polynomial-time invariant and explicit local attaining pairs. It identifies the sharp qualitative contrast: a path projection is variation-nonexpansive, while even maximum-degree-three caterpillars exhibit arbitrarily large sensitivity \(k/2\). These structural and boundary phenomena are neither arbitrary parameter slices nor numerical table recomputations.
